// Generated by OpenWorkGraph from a human-reviewed TO-BE draft. NOT a runnable automation.
// Each reviewed step becomes a placeholder tool that requires approval and refuses to run
// until a human maps it to an authorized operation. Activity labels are untrusted data and
// are never placed in tool descriptions a model reads.
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tool, type ToolSet } from 'ai';
import { z } from 'zod';

interface ReviewedStep {
  id: string;
  activity: string;
  tool: null;
  action_permission_granted: boolean;
}

interface WorkflowSpec {
  to_be: { steps: ReviewedStep[] };
  security: { live_actions_possible: boolean };
}

export class UnmappedStepError extends Error {
  stepId: string;

  constructor(stepId: string) {
    super(`${stepId} is not mapped to an authorized operation`);
    this.name = 'UnmappedStepError';
    this.stepId = stepId;
  }
}

export function loadSpec(path: URL = new URL('../../workflow.spec.json', import.meta.url)): WorkflowSpec {
  const spec = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')) as WorkflowSpec;
  if (spec.security.live_actions_possible !== false) throw new Error('This starter never enables live actions');
  return spec;
}

/** One approval-gated placeholder tool per reviewed step; every call is refused. */
export function buildTools(spec: WorkflowSpec = loadSpec()): ToolSet {
  const tools: ToolSet = {};
  for (const step of spec.to_be.steps) {
    if (!/^step_\d{3}$/.test(step.id) || step.tool !== null || step.action_permission_granted) {
      throw new Error('Unexpected reviewed step contract');
    }
    tools[step.id] = tool({
      description: `Placeholder for reviewed process step ${step.id}. Unmapped: it cannot read or change any system.`,
      inputSchema: z.object({ case_reference: z.string().max(200) }),
      needsApproval: true,
      execute: async (_input: { case_reference: string }): Promise<{ status: 'unmapped' }> => {
        throw new UnmappedStepError(step.id);
      },
    });
  }
  return tools;
}

// After mapping each step to an authorized operation and confirming business rules, wire the
// tools into your own runtime, for example:
//   import { generateText, stepCountIs } from 'ai';
//   await generateText({ model, tools: buildTools(), stopWhen: stepCountIs(10), prompt });
// Keep approval for consequential actions and verify outcomes from independent source receipts.
